@@ -68,0 +69,10 @@ describe('List', () => {
+
+  test('partition', () => {
+    expect(List.partition((x: number) => x > 1, [1, 2, 3])).toEqual(Tuple([2, 3], [1]))
+    expect(List.partition((x: number) => x > 1)([1, 2, 3])).toEqual(Tuple([2, 3], [1]))
+    expect(List.partition((x: number) => x > 1, [])).toEqual(Tuple([], []))
+    expect(List.partition((x: number) => x > 1)([])).toEqual(Tuple([], []))
+    expect(List.partition((x: number) => x % 2 === 0, [1, 2, 3, 4])).toEqual(Tuple([2, 4], [1, 3]))
+    expect(List.partition(() => true, [1, 2])).toEqual(Tuple([1, 2], []))
+    expect(List.partition(() => false, [1, 2])).toEqual(Tuple([], [1, 2]))
+  })

@@ -80,0 +81,24 @@ function at<T>(index: number, list?: readonly T[]): any {
+/** Returns a tuple of arrays: the first contains elements that pass the predicate, the second those that do not. Both maintain original order. */
+function partition<T>(
+  f: (x: T, index: number, arr: T[]) => boolean,
+  list: readonly T[]
+): Tuple<T[], T[]>
+function partition<T>(
+  f: (x: T, index: number, arr: T[]) => boolean
+): (list: readonly T[]) => Tuple<T[], T[]>
+function partition<T>(
+  f: (x: T, index: number, arr: T[]) => boolean,
+  list?: readonly T[]
+): any {
+  switch (arguments.length) {
+    case 1:
+      return (list: readonly T[]) => partition(f, list)
+    default:
+      const res: T[][] = [[], []]
+      list!.forEach((x) =>
+        f(x) ? res[0].push(x) : res[1].push(x)
+      )
+      return Tuple(res[0], res[1])
+  }
+}
